Automated checks

Source: vignettes/articles/checks.Rmd
checks.Rmd

Three checks run on every pull request and every push to main (.github/workflows/checks.yml). Each is a script you can run locally from the repo root.

Check What it proves Run locally
db db/ loads into an empty PostgreSQL in one session. Smoke checks: a new project gets an access key, a new curve gets its multiplate group, every view and settings function the app and worker use runs, the settings cascade returns the system defaults, schema_version is 0.7.0 db/tests/load_test.sh /usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin (the folder holding initdb, pg_ctl, psql)
manifests Every manifest and the Compose file parse. Every secretKeyRef names a Secret the manifests define. Every IMMUNOPLEX_* placeholder is filled by the sed step in the cluster install guide. Every image is listed in the air-gapped install guide. Every ghcr.io/immunoplex image is pinned (release tag or digest). The Compose file uses the same I-SPI and i-spi-compute versions as the manifests python3 tests/check_manifests.py (needs PyYAML)
e2e The local stack (local/docker-compose.yml) does a real fit. Steps below tests/e2e/run_e2e.sh

The e2e steps: 1. Start the stack on an empty database. 2. Seed a small synthetic study (tests/e2e/seed.sql): 2 plates; 8 standard dilutions in duplicate; blanks, controls and samples. 3. Submit a frequentist fit to the compute API, as I-SPI does. 4. Wait for the job to finish. 5. Check what the worker wrote (tests/e2e/check.sql): - the run with its release manifest; - the best model per curve, parameters, grid and diagnostics; - all 8 samples; - all 32 standards with their stored estimates; - the blanks; - all 8 controls.

Before running the e2e test locally: - It deletes the local stack’s data: it runs docker compose down -v before and after. - KEEP_STACK=1 leaves the stack running afterwards, for inspection. - On Windows, set PYTHON=python. - The first run downloads the images, about 8 GB. - The fit itself takes seconds.

A fourth workflow, .github/workflows/pkgdown.yml, builds this site on every pull request and publishes it from main.
